citations.authors: Webster JB, Crunkhorn A, Sall J, Highsmith MJ, Pruziner A, Randolph BJ
citations.title: Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Rehabilitation of Lower Limb Amputation: An Update from the Department of Veterans Affairs and Department of Defense
citations.journal: American Journal of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation
citations.what_it_says: Updated VA/DoD CPG codifying interdisciplinary team care, staged rehabilitation, and outcome-measure-driven prosthetic training as the standard of care.

citations.authors: Highsmith MJ, Andrews CR, Millman C, et al.
citations.title: Gait Training Interventions for Lower Extremity Amputees: A Systematic Literature Review
citations.what_it_says: Review of 18 studies: overground gait training with verbal/manual augmentation and treadmill-based training are effective at improving prosthetic gait.

citations.authors: Wong CK, Ehrlich JE, Ersing JC, et al.
citations.title: Exercise programs to improve gait performance in people with lower limb amputation: A systematic review
citations.what_it_says: Exercise programs emphasizing resisted gait and functional training produced small-to-large effect-size improvements in gait performance.

citations.authors: Abou L, Fliflet A, Zhao L, Du Y, Rice L
citations.title: The Effectiveness of Exercise Interventions to Improve Gait and Balance in Individuals with Lower Limb Amputations: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
citations.what_it_says: Meta-analysis of 15 RCTs (n=594): exercise interventions significantly improve gait and balance in people with lower limb amputation.

citations.authors: Stineman MG, Kwong PL, Kurichi JE, et al.
citations.title: The effectiveness of inpatient rehabilitation in the acute postoperative phase of care after transtibial or transfemoral amputation: study of an integrated health care delivery system
citations.journal: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation
citations.what_it_says: In 2,673 veterans, acute postoperative inpatient rehabilitation was associated with higher 1-year survival, home discharge, and prosthetic procurement.

citations.authors: Pezzin LE, Dillingham TR, MacKenzie EJ
citations.title: Rehabilitation and the long-term outcomes of persons with trauma-related amputations
citations.journal: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation
citations.what_it_says: Inpatient rehabilitation intensity was associated with better long-term physical function, vocational outcomes, and health status in trauma-related amputees.

citations.authors: Gailey RS, Roach KE, Applegate EB, et al.
citations.title: The Amputee Mobility Predictor: an instrument to assess determinants of the lower-limb amputee's ability to ambulate
citations.journal: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation
citations.what_it_says: Develops and validates the Amputee Mobility Predictor, the instrument underpinning Medicare K-level classification and PT-led prosthetic candidacy assessment.

citations.authors: Wurdeman SR, Stevens PM, Campbell JH
citations.title: Mobility Analysis of AmpuTees (MAAT I): Quality of life and satisfaction are strongly related to mobility for patients with a lower limb prosthesis
citations.what_it_says: Mobility (PLUS-M) strongly correlated with quality of life and satisfaction in a large clinical sample of lower limb prosthesis users.

citations.authors: Sansam K, Neumann V, O'Connor R, Bhakta B
citations.title: Predicting walking ability following lower limb amputation: a systematic review of the literature
citations.what_it_says: Review of 57 studies identifying cognition, fitness, balance, and pre-operative mobility as predictors of prosthetic walking ability.

citations.authors: van Velzen JM, van Bennekom CA, Polomski W, et al.
citations.title: Physical capacity and walking ability after lower limb amputation: a systematic review
citations.what_it_says: Strong evidence that balance and physical capacity relate to walking ability after amputation, supporting pre-prosthetic conditioning.

citations.authors: Highsmith MJ, Kahle JT, Miro RM, et al.
citations.title: Prosthetic interventions for people with transtibial amputation: Systematic review and meta-analysis of high-quality prospective literature and systematic reviews
citations.journal: Journal of Rehabilitation Research and Development
citations.what_it_says: Synthesizes 31 high-quality studies into evidence statements on prosthetic components, postoperative care, and alignment for transtibial amputees.

citations.authors: Heyns A, Jacobs S, Negrini S, et al.
citations.title: Systematic Review of Clinical Practice Guidelines for Individuals With Amputation: Identification of Best Evidence for Rehabilitation to Develop the WHO's Package of Interventions for Rehabilitation
citations.journal: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation
citations.what_it_says: WHO-commissioned review: only 6.9% of amputee-rehabilitation guideline recommendations are grounded in RCTs or systematic reviews; quantifying the field's evidence ceiling.

citations.authors: Christiansen CL, Miller MJ, Murray AM, Stephenson RO, Stevens-Lapsley JE, Hiatt WR, Schenkman ML
citations.title: Behavior-Change Intervention Targeting Physical Function and Walking Activity After Dysvascular Amputation: A Randomized Controlled Trial
citations.what_it_says: An OUTPATIENT evidence-based amputee rehabilitation program targeting physical function and community walking improved outcomes after lower-limb amputation, showing the prosthetic-training caseload extends well beyond the acute/inpatient setting.
